note: A BENEFIT case that FAILS, and it is kept because of what it shows. Context supplied 'Brindlewood' and 'quillmark-sync' reliably (3/3 each), but 'Kaelith' comes back as 'Keyleth' even with the correct spelling on screen three times. 'Keyleth' is a name the model already knows; 'Kaelith' is not. So grounding transfers a novel spelling only when nothing in the model's own vocabulary competes for the same sound -- when something does, the learned token wins over the screen. This is the same failure the project was started to fix, one level down: not a user dictionary overriding the speaker, but the model's own. Fix it and this becomes a passing case; until then it is the honest boundary of what grounding does.
